title: FileId/span integrity: findings from the q2 source-span audit (parse_with_parent contract, FileId(0) aliasing, validation-crate context mismatches)
description:
During a systematic audit of FileId/span integrity in Quarto 2 (triggered by a wrong-file diagnostic-span bug, quarto-dev/q2#478), we traced several weaknesses to APIs in this workspace. Recording them here for visibility since the audit itself lives in q2's (non-public) issue tracker. **We are addressing these as part of a planned redesign of the quarto-source-map binding API** (making the (FileId, offsets, content) pairing unrepresentable-when-wrong); the items below will mostly ride that work rather than being patched piecemeal. Filing so readers of this repo know the problems are known and owned.

## quarto-yaml

**Y1 — `parse_with_parent`'s contract is unchecked, and the doc example violates it.**
The parent `SourceInfo` must describe exactly the `content` being parsed (origin at byte 0 of `content`, length = `content.len()`), but nothing validates this: `make_source_info` stores offsets verbatim into `SourceInfo::substring`, and `resolve_byte_range` composes `parent_start + offset` with no clamp to the parent's end. A misaligned parent yields plausible in-file offsets at the wrong location. The doc example on `parse_with_parent` (parser.rs, the `rust,no_run` block) narrates "extracted from parent document at offset 10–50" while passing a parent spanning `0..1000` — every resulting span would be off by 10. Suggested minimal fix ahead of the redesign: `debug_assert!(parent.length() == content.len())` in `parse_impl` + correct the example.

**Y2 — the `FileId(0)` dummy aliases real files.**
`parse()` (no filename, no parent) mints `Original { FileId(0), … }` for every node (`make_source_info`, `make_source_info_at_offset`, `make_tag_source_info`). Because `quarto_source_map::SourceContext::get_file` falls back to positional indexing for unmapped ids, a dummy span resolves *successfully* against whatever file was registered first in the consumer's context — a confidently wrong span rather than a missing one. Direction: mint a reserved non-aliasing sentinel (or `file_id_for_filename("<anonymous>")`) instead of 0; the sentinel arrives with the quarto-source-map redesign.

**Y4 — `file_id_for_filename` truncates to 32 bits on wasm32.**
`hasher.finish() as usize` halves the hash width on wasm32 targets. Combined with `SourceContext::add_file_with_id` panicking on duplicate ids, a birthday collision (~2^16 registered filenames) becomes a crash in WASM consumers. The redesigned API plans a width-stable id and non-panicking duplicate handling; noting here because the hash recipe is documented as a stability contract.

## quarto-yaml-validation

**V1 — nothing ties a diagnostic to the `SourceContext` it is rendered with.**
`ValidationDiagnostic::from_validation_error(err, ctx_A)` computes ranges with one context while `to_text(&self, ctx_B)` renders with whatever context the caller passes later; `ValidationError::with_yaml_node(node, ctx)` likewise accepts any ctx for any node. Constructing with one context and rendering with another is fully representable and produces byte offsets rendered against the wrong file's content (the exact bug class the q2 audit chased). Direction: a single owning handle so construction and rendering cannot see different contexts.

**V2 — `SourceRange` mixes coordinate spaces.**
In `diagnostic.rs` (`source_range` construction): `filename` comes from the fully-resolved root file, but `start_offset`/`end_offset` come from `SourceInfo::start_offset()`/`end_offset()`, which are **parent-relative** for every `Substring` (i.e. every parsed node). This is coincidentally correct for `parse_file` (parent spans the whole file from 0) and wrong for `parse_with_parent`: a frontmatter diagnostic reports the parent document's filename with offsets relative to the frontmatter, while `start_line`/`start_column` in the same struct are correct. Any JSON consumer slicing the named file at those offsets reads the wrong text. Fix: derive the offsets from `resolve_byte_range()` so they share a base with `filename`. (Also: `end_offset() - start_offset()` underflow-panics in debug for hand-built spans with `end < start`; `SourceInfo::original` never validates ordering.)

**V3 — the filename hash is re-implemented inline in `diagnostic.rs` test helpers** instead of calling the public `file_id_for_filename`, which parser.rs documents as the stability contract. A hash-recipe change would silently desynchronize them.

## Non-issues verified while auditing

- Schema-file spans cannot leak into instance diagnostics through the normal path: `Schema` discards spans after parsing and all `add_error` sites pass instance nodes.
- `create_contiguous_span`'s same-file assert is unreachable today (single builder, fixed parent) — though the `Substring` arm silently drops `end_info`'s parent and would mint a hybrid span if per-node parents ever appear; an assert there would restore symmetry.

Happy to expand any of these into separate actionable issues when the redesign plan lands; treat this one as the umbrella/context record.

title: YAML tags on sequences and mappings are discarded (only scalars capture tags)
description:
## Summary

`quarto_yaml::parse_file` only captures YAML tags on **scalar** nodes. Tags written on sequences or mappings are silently discarded: `Event::SequenceStart` and `Event::MappingStart` receive the tag from the parser but ignore it.

In `src/parser.rs` (v0.1.1):

- `Event::Scalar(value, style, _anchor_id, tag)` (line 408) — tag captured, span located via `find_tag_span`, attached to the node.
- `Event::SequenceStart(_anchor_id, _tag)` (line 440) — **tag discarded**.
- `Event::MappingStart(_anchor_id, _tag)` (line 470) — **tag discarded**.

## Repro

```rust
let yaml = quarto_yaml::parse_file("k: !prefer\n  - a\n", "repro.yml").unwrap();
// Walk the tree: no node anywhere carries `tag: Some(..)`.
```

Same for the flow form `k: !prefer [a]` and for tagged mappings (`k: !prefer\n  x: 1`). A tagged scalar (`k: !str a`) works as expected.

## Impact (downstream: quarto-dev/q2)

Quarto 2's config-merge machinery (`quarto-config`'s `MergedConfig`) implements `!prefer` / `!concat` semantics for arrays and maps, and its YAML→ConfigValue conversion reads `YamlWithSourceInfo.tag` to set the merge op. Because this crate never attaches tags to non-scalar nodes, **`!prefer` / `!concat` written on an array or map in any user YAML file is a silent no-op** — the merge layer supports it, but the tag never arrives. Scalars are unaffected (they default to last-wins anyway), so the bug precisely nullifies the tags on the node shapes where they matter most.

We hit this implementing extension-contributed custom project types, where `!prefer` on a list (e.g. `include-in-header`) is the documented way for a project to *replace* an extension-contributed default instead of concatenating with it. Tracked in q2 as strand `bd-43lc07w1`; a regression test pinning the desired behavior is checked in there as `#[ignore]` pending this fix (`crates/quarto-core/tests/integration/custom_project_type.rs`, `user_prefer_replaces_extension_array`).

## Assessment / suggested fix

1. In `on_event`, capture the tag in `SequenceStart` / `MappingStart` and stash it on the corresponding `BuildNode::Sequence` / `BuildNode::Mapping` frame, then attach it to the built node in `SequenceEnd` / `MappingEnd`.
2. The tag-span discovery (`find_tag_span`, currently anchored to the scalar's value marker) needs a collection-flavored variant: for block collections the tag precedes the first item/entry (often on the parent key's line, e.g. `k: !prefer`), so the search window differs from the scalar case. The existing fallback path (guess from suffix length, stay in-bounds) is a reasonable interim for collections too.
3. `YamlWithSourceInfo` already has the `tag: Option<(String, SourceInfo)>` field and constructors for scalars (`new_scalar_with_tag`); `new_array` / `new_hash` need tag-carrying variants (or a `with_tag` builder).

Happy to provide more downstream context if useful.

title: Flow-collection spans exclude the closing bracket
Spans are built from character indices but consumed as byte offsets
description:
`SourceInfo` spans are documented and consumed as byte offsets, but they are built from `yaml_rust2::Marker::index()`, which counts **characters**. The two agree only while the document is ASCII: one multi-byte character shifts every later span left by its extra bytes, so spans no longer line up with the source they came from.

## Reprex

`Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[dependencies]
quarto-yaml = "0.1.1"
```

`src/main.rs`:

```rust
use quarto_yaml::parse_file;

fn show(content: &str) {
    println!("--- {content:?}");
    let doc = parse_file(content, "test.yaml").unwrap();
    for entry in doc.as_hash().unwrap() {
        let key = entry.key.yaml.as_str().unwrap();
        let (_, start, end) = entry.value.source_info.resolve_byte_range().unwrap();
        println!("  {key}: span {start}..{end} -> {:?}", content.get(start..end));
    }
}

fn main() {
    show("first: plain\nsecond: \"quoted\"\n");
    show("first: é\nsecond: \"quoted\"\n");
}
```

Output — the two documents differ only in the value of `first`:

```
--- "first: plain\nsecond: \"quoted\"\n"
  first: span 7..12 -> Some("plain")
  second: span 21..29 -> Some("\"quoted\"")
--- "first: é\nsecond: \"quoted\"\n"
  first: span 7..9 -> Some("é")
  second: span 17..23 -> Some(" \"quot")
```

`second`'s span should be `20..28` (`"quoted"`). It is off in both endpoints: shifted one byte left by the `é`, and two bytes short.

A span that lands inside a multi-byte character makes it worse — `content.get(start..end)` then returns `None`, and a caller slicing directly would panic.

## Cause

`yaml-rust2`'s `Marker` stores a character index (`scanner.rs`, field `index`: *"The index (in chars) in the input string"*), though its `index()` getter is documented as *"Return the index (in bytes)"* — that contradiction looks like the origin of the bug, and is worth reporting there too.

The parser takes it as a byte offset in four places:

- `make_source_info` / `make_source_info_at_offset` (`parser.rs:278`, `:297`) use `marker.index()` as the span's start.
- `compute_scalar_len` (`parser.rs:317`) does `self.source.get(start..)` with it. Once a multi-byte character precedes the scalar, that slice starts in the wrong place, so `plain_scalar_len`/`quoted_scalar_len` fail to match and every scalar length silently falls back to `value.len()` — which is why the quoted scalar above lost its quotes.
- `find_tag_span` (`parser.rs:349`) slices `self.source` the same way (and returns `None` outright if the index isn't a char boundary).
- Collection spans take their length as a *difference* of marker indices (`parser.rs:456`, `:518`, `:523`), i.e. in characters.

The last two points mean the units aren't just wrong, they're inconsistent: after the first multi-byte character, scalar lengths are byte counts while collection lengths are character counts. So fixing only the start offsets wouldn't be enough — the lengths have to be measured in bytes too.

## Impact

Everything downstream indexes bytes: `quarto-source-map`'s `FileInfo` builds its line index from byte offsets of newlines, so a shifted span resolves to a wrong row/column, and renderers like `annotate-snippets` take byte ranges into the source. In practice a single em dash or smart quote anywhere earlier in a file moves every subsequent diagnostic — often onto a different line entirely, which is worse than reporting no location at all. Front matter with typographic punctuation is common enough that this is easy to hit.

## Suggested fix

Convert the marker's character index to a byte offset once, at the parser boundary — e.g. track the byte position alongside the scanner's char index, or keep a char → byte table for the source — and use byte offsets consistently for both span endpoints, including the collection lengths.

Found while chasing misreported diagnostic locations in [data-dict](https://github.com/tidyverse/data-dict/issues/153). Versions: quarto-yaml 0.1.1, quarto-source-map 0.1.0, yaml-rust2 0.11.0.

title: Plain `0x1f` / `0o17` resolve to strings, not integers
description:
`resolve_plain_scalar` (`src/parser.rs`) tries `i64::from_str`, then a float, then the bool/null spellings, and falls through to `String`. `i64::from_str` only accepts decimal, so the YAML 1.2 core schema's hexadecimal and octal integer forms end up as strings.

Per the [core schema](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#103-core-schema), `!!int` matches `[-+]?[0-9]+`, `0o[0-7]+` **and** `0x[0-9a-fA-F]+`. yaml-rust2's own `Yaml::from_str` handles both prefixed forms.

## Reproduction

| Input | quarto-yaml | yaml-rust2 | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x1f` | `String("0x1f")` | `Integer(31)` | `Integer(31)` |
| `0xFF` | `String("0xFF")` | `Integer(255)` | `Integer(255)` |
| `0o17` | `String("0o17")` | `Integer(15)` | `Integer(15)` |

Cases that are already right, and should stay that way — the core schema's prefixed forms are lower-case and unsigned, so these three are genuinely strings:

| Input | Resolves to |
|---|---|
| `0X1f` | `String("0X1f")` |
| `-0x1f` | `String("-0x1f")` |
| `0b101` | `String("0b101")` (no binary form in the core schema) |

## Knock-on effect

An explicit `!!int` tag on a hex or octal value resolves to `Yaml::BadValue`, because `resolve_tagged_scalar` also goes through `i64::from_str`:

```
k: !!int 0x1f   =>  BadValue
k: !!int 0o17   =>  BadValue
```

So a fix wants to land in one shared "parse a core-schema integer" helper used by both the tagged and untagged paths.

Found while fixing #2, which reworked scalar resolution in this code path but deliberately left this divergence alone.

title: Quoted scalars are re-typed from their text, so `"1"` parses as an integer
Expose more of the `annotate-snippets` API
description:
Things I'd find useful:

* https://docs.rs/annotate-snippets/latest/annotate_snippets/enum.AnnotationKind.html#variant.Visible — so you can have multiple visible lines of context
* https://docs.rs/annotate-snippets/latest/annotate_snippets/struct.Patch.html — so you can emit specific advice for changes
